Definition: from ὄστρακον ("oyster") (a tile, i.e. terra cotta); earthen-ware, i.e. clayey; by implication, frail:--of earth, earthen.
BiblicalUsage: Earthen means made of clay. Paul says we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of God and not of us, and that in a great house there are vessels of gold and silver, and also of wood and of earth.
TheologicalSignificance: What I hold is that the earthen vessel is the point: the treasure is in a clay jar on purpose, so that the power is seen to be God's, not mine.
